nodes.text: 23:30... Danas je točno šest mjeseci otkako mi je dijagnosticiran rak, bolest koja se neprimjetno širila mojim tijelom dok sam imao samo dosadan kašalj.

nodes.source: This time on the 9th of December 2004 I was lying in a medical assessment unit in West Middlesex Hospital, riddled with disease. My friends had gone home and I was left to wonder, alone in my room, what the future would hold for me.
nodes.text: Na današnji dan, 9. prosinca 2004., u ovo vrijeme ležao sam na odjelu za medicinsku procjenu u bolnici West Middlesex, s rakom raširenim po tijelu. Prijatelji su otišli kući, a ja sam ostao sam u sobi pitajući se što mi budućnost donosi.

nodes.source: So, half a year later, I have been through 4 cycles of extensive BEP chemotherapy followed by major surgery and today I'm in remission from a Cancer that almost killed me. My story has been told and you've all been here to share it with me.
nodes.text: Šest mjeseci poslije prošao sam četiri opsežna ciklusa BEP kemoterapije i veliku operaciju, a danas sam u remisiji raka koji me zamalo ubio. Ispričao sam svoju priču, a svi ste bili ovdje da je podijelite sa mnom.

nodes.source: Strangely on this anniversary, a documentary was aired this evening called "Bollocks to Cancer". A documentary about a young Testicular Cancer sufferer and survivor. Although a different person and a short production to pack a lot of experience in to, it really brought back some vivid memories and experiences for me.
nodes.text: Neobično, baš na ovu obljetnicu večeras je prikazan dokumentarac 'Bollocks to Cancer' o mladom muškarcu koji je obolio od raka testisa i preživio ga. Iako govori o drugoj osobi i u kratkom vremenu pokušava prikazati mnogo toga, probudio mi je vrlo žive uspomene i iskustva.

nodes.source: It certainly did a good job of portraying what it's like to lie in hospital on BEP chemotherapy, the thought processes and feelings. My treatment was the exactly the same, I had an extra cycle. The wards were similar in layout although I did not have other Testicular Cancer sufferers around me. At the beginning, in one of my earlier male ward stays, all five of my fellow patients died. That was tough.
nodes.text: Doista je dobro prikazao kako izgleda ležati u bolnici na BEP kemoterapiji, razmišljanja i osjećaje. Moje je liječenje bilo praktički jednako, samo sam imao jedan ciklus više. Odjeli su izgledali slično, premda oko mene nije bilo drugih pacijenata s rakom testisa. Na početku, na jednom od prvih muških odjela na kojima sam ležao, svih pet pacijenata oko mene umrlo je. To je bilo teško.

nodes.source: I have a different perspective on life now and have learnt a great lesson in mortality. A gift if you like, but not exactly the best way to receive it. It's difficult to describe the feeling, you have to experience it in one way or another for yourself, something which I do not wish on anyone.
nodes.text: Sada drukčije gledam na život i naučio sam veliku lekciju o smrtnosti. Dar, ako ga tako želite nazvati, ali ne baš najbolji način da ga dobiješ. Taj je osjećaj teško opisati; moraš ga na neki način sam doživjeti, što nikome ne bih poželio.

nodes.source: My website lives on, as I do. I will be back soon with more information on further scans and tests that I am to have.
nodes.text: Moja internetska stranica nastavlja živjeti, baš kao i ja. Uskoro ću se vratiti s informacijama o daljnjim snimanjima i pretragama koje me čekaju.

nodes.source: July 2005
nodes.text: srpanj 2005.

nodes.source: Arrived at the hospital very much on time this morning, the traffic was a breeze.
nodes.text: Jutros sam stigao u bolnicu sasvim na vrijeme, promet je bio lagan.

nodes.source: As instructed by phone earlier in the week I went straight to Clinic 8 for my X-Ray form and then to the MRI reception to register my attendance in good time for the MRI scan.
nodes.text: Prema telefonskim uputama ranije ovog tjedna, otišao sam ravno u ambulantu broj 8 po uputnicu za rendgen, a zatim na prijam za MR kako bih se pravodobno prijavio za snimanje.

nodes.source: After registering at the MRI reception I went for my X-Ray. A very jolly bunch of nurses were operating the X-Ray machine today, I had a bit of a laugh and showed them my website. Although a serious condition I am monitoring with all of these X-Rays and tests, it's nice to have a bit of a laugh, normally at my expense... just to keep the spirits high, which is just as they should be!
nodes.text: Nakon prijave na MR otišao sam na rendgen. Danas je aparatom upravljala vesela skupina medicinskih sestara. Malo smo se šalili i pokazao sam im svoju stranicu. Iako ovim snimanjima i pretragama pratim ozbiljnu bolest, lijepo se malo nasmijati, obično na vlastiti račun, kako bi raspoloženje ostalo visoko!

nodes.source: Straight after the X-Ray I went through for my MRI scan. My second MRI ever and I had the pleasure of putting a new scanner through its paces. I took a photo of the scanner (check the gallery soon), apparently it's worth 750,000 pounds sterling! I could certainly think of a few things to buy with that amount of money! However in this instance I think it's probably money well spent!
nodes.text: Odmah nakon rendgena otišao sam na MR. Moj drugi MR u životu i imao sam zadovoljstvo isprobati potpuno novi uređaj. Fotografirao sam ga, uskoro pogledajte galeriju. Navodno vrijedi 750.000 funti! Za taj bih novac mogao smisliti mnogo toga što bih kupio! Ali u ovom je slučaju vjerojatno pametno potrošen!

nodes.source: The X-Ray was to check up on my lungs and the MRI was a followup from my report to the Doctor that my hips/legs were giving off a creaking sensation which comes and goes at no particular time.
nodes.text: Rendgen je služio provjeri pluća, a MR je bio kontrola zbog osjećaja škripanja u kukovima i nogama koji sam prijavio liječniku i koji se pojavljuje bez očitog pravila.

nodes.source: After my thorough zapping this morning it was off to Clinic 8 for my regular blood tests. This was quite quick and relatively painless (I am really getting used to these).
nodes.text: Nakon jutrošnjeg temeljitog 'zračenja' otišao sam u ambulantu broj 8 na rutinske krvne pretrage. Bilo je brzo i razmjerno bezbolno, doista se već navikavam.

nodes.source: Following a short wait I was seen by my Consultant, Dr. Savage. He had by that time had a chance to go over the scans from earlier today and was pleased to announce that they were all in order. Whatever they had suspected might be up with me as a serious Chemotherapy side effect was not the case and everything looked normal. I'll just have to put up with the creaking sensation and hope that it goes away sooner rather than later. Just as with the other side effects I have accepted and am dealing with on a daily basis.
nodes.text: Nakon kratkog čekanja primio me specijalist dr. Savage. Do tada je pregledao današnje snimke i sa zadovoljstvom objavio da je sve uredno. Ono na što su sumnjali kao na ozbiljnu nuspojavu kemoterapije nije se potvrdilo, sve izgleda normalno. Morat ću se nositi sa škripanjem i nadati se da će prije ili poslije prestati, kao i s drugim nuspojavama koje sam prihvatio i podnosim svaki dan.

nodes.source: The X-Ray was also as clear as expected, there is damage to my lungs which is more apparent on a CT scan, however nothing nasty shows and in time they will hopefully get a lot better. I cannot really say that I notice any difference but then I haven't put any great amount of pressure on them yet. Just a couple of mountain bike rides out along the river which I seem to cope with very well, perhaps even better than before... but back then I suppose I was riding with developing tumours in my lungs that I didn't even realise I had!
nodes.text: Rendgen je također bio čist kako se očekivalo. Na plućima ima oštećenja koja su vidljivija na CT-u, ali ništa zloćudno nije se pokazalo i s vremenom bi trebala biti mnogo bolja. Ne mogu reći da primjećujem razliku, ali još ih nisam ozbiljno opteretio. Odradio sam tek nekoliko vožnji brdskim biciklom uz rijeku i podnio ih vrlo dobro, možda čak bolje nego prije. Premda sam prije, valjda, vozio dok su mi u plućima rasli tumori za koje nisam ni znao!

nodes.source: I then paid a quick visit to the various wards that I have been treated in over the past months. It's nice to see the people who have treated me and give them a healthy smile, it makes them happy to know that 'the person' or 'the number' they treated is well again as quite often the case is that they hardly ever get to see patients again whatever the outcome. It also gives me good vibes to see them so happy that I am better and looking so much more healthy again.
nodes.text: Zatim sam nakratko obišao različite odjele na kojima sam se liječio proteklih mjeseci. Lijepo je vidjeti ljude koji su me liječili i široko im se nasmiješiti kao zdrava osoba. Njima mnogo znači znati da je 'osoba' ili 'broj' kojega su liječili opet dobro, jer često više nikad ne vide pacijenta, bez obzira na ishod. I meni daje dobar osjećaj vidjeti koliko se vesele što sam ozdravio i opet izgledam mnogo zdravije.

nodes.source: All in all quite a busy day at the hospital today. A small error in my blood test schedules has been rectified and I am now on a fortnightly regime as you will see from my updated schedule. Soon it will switch to monthly.
nodes.text: Sve u svemu, danas je bio prilično zaposlen dan u bolnici. Ispravljena je mala pogreška u rasporedu krvnih pretraga i sada dolazim svaka dva tjedna, kao što ćete vidjeti u ažuriranom rasporedu. Uskoro će biti jednom mjesečno.

nodes.source: Unless anything exciting happens, I'll be back again on the 12th to report on my findings with the surgeon's team.
nodes.text: Ako se ne dogodi nešto uzbudljivo, vraćam se 12. srpnja s novostima nakon susreta s kirurškim timom.

nodes.source: In the meantime I'll be making some changes and updates to the site so watch this space.
nodes.text: U međuvremenu ću mijenjati i ažurirati stranicu, pa pratite novosti.

nodes.source: 12th July 2005 - Tuesday
nodes.text: 12. srpnja 2005. - utorak

nodes.source: I came in to the hospital today for a pre arranged meeting with one of the Surgeon's team. Something that I had arranged for once, to clear up some outstanding queries.
nodes.text: Danas sam došao u bolnicu na unaprijed dogovoren sastanak s članom kirurškog tima. Ovoga puta sam ga sam dogovorio da razjasnim nekoliko preostalih pitanja.

nodes.source: The scars are healing well although it'll be sometime indeed before they fade from the red lines that currently show. I have some numbness around and below my groin scar site (the Orchiectomy scar), this is totally normal and to be expected.
nodes.text: Ožiljci dobro zacjeljuju, iako će proći još dosta vremena prije nego što crvene crte izblijede. Oko i ispod ožiljka u preponi, od orhiektomije, imam malo utrnulosti. To je sasvim normalno i očekivano.

nodes.source: The clips... well this is something that I feel has still not been put to bed properly. For one thing I was told I cannot physically have one (just so I can show you all and for a reference as to what I have inside me). The other and more important factor is that there are no notes on exactly how many of these clips were used or their locations within my body.
nodes.text: Kirurške kopčice... to je nešto što još uvijek smatram nerazjašnjenim. Prvo, rekli su mi da fizički ne mogu dobiti jednu, samo kako bih vam je pokazao i imao primjer onoga što nosim u sebi. Drugo, što je važnije, nema nikakve zabilješke o tome koliko je kopčica upotrijebljeno ni gdje su smještene u mojem tijelu.

nodes.source: In fact and according to the doctor I saw today, there are no notes on my surgery or the procedure whatsoever, I find this odd.
nodes.text: Zapravo, prema liječniku kojeg sam danas vidio, nema nikakvih bilješki o mojoj operaciji ili postupku. To mi je neobično.

nodes.source: I did manage to find out that the clips are made of a type of plastic called Silastic with titanium hinges, but even then the doctor was vague about this.
nodes.text: Uspio sam saznati da su kopčice izrađene od vrste plastike zvane Silastic s titanijskim šarkama, premda ni u to liječnik nije bio sasvim siguran.

nodes.source: 15th July 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 15. srpnja 2005. - petak

nodes.source: My first blood test in another hospital.
nodes.text: Prvo vađenje krvi u drugoj bolnici.

nodes.source: I had a meeting today at the Mulberry Centre so I thought it best to get my routine blood test carried out at West Middlesex Hospital as it is right next door and very local to where I live!
nodes.text: Danas sam imao sastanak u Mulberry Centreu pa sam odlučio rutinsku krvnu pretragu obaviti u bolnici West Middlesex, odmah pokraj centra i vrlo blizu mojeg doma!

nodes.source: An all new environment to me so I asked at main reception where the outpatients blood test department was. I was swiftly and accurately directed.
nodes.text: Okruženje mi je bilo sasvim novo pa sam na glavnom prijamu pitao gdje je ambulantni laboratorij za vađenje krvi. Brzo su me i točno uputili.

nodes.source: Most of West Middlesex Hospital is now relatively new buildings and the blood test department appeared clean and new. The nurses were chatty, they were so quiet I had to knock on the door and butt in on their gossip in order to get my blood test done.
nodes.text: Većina zgrada bolnice West Middlesex danas je razmjerno nova, a odjel za vađenje krvi izgledao je čist i moderan. Sestre su bile brbljave, a ondje je bilo toliko mirno da sam morao pokucati i upasti im u razgovor kako bih došao na red za vađenje krvi.

nodes.source: All in all a nice experience in what was a foreign environment for me. I'll be coming back for more blood tests here in the future!
nodes.text: Sve u svemu, ugodno iskustvo u meni nepoznatom okruženju. Ubuduće ću ovdje dolaziti na još krvnih pretraga!

nodes.source: August 2005
nodes.text: kolovoz 2005.

nodes.source: 5th August 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 5. kolovoza 2005. - petak

nodes.source: Routine blood test and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danas rutinska krvna pretraga i sastanak s mojim konzultantom u bolnici Charing Cross.

nodes.source: Everything looking good so far, my markers remain at normal and full blood count results now fall within the normal values although still at the bottom end of the spectrum.
nodes.text: Zasad sve izgleda dobro. Tumorski biljezi ostaju u granicama normale, a kompletna krvna slika sada je također u normalnim vrijednostima, iako još pri donjoj granici raspona.

nodes.source: Physical examination carried out, all good.
nodes.text: Obavljen je i fizički pregled, sve je dobro.

nodes.source: After the meeting I was sent for an additional blood test to check my testosterone levels, this is a new one for me. I told the Phlebotomist to be careful with the tube of blood he took as it may blow the testing machine up if they are not careful. I haven't noticed any of the low testosterone symptoms as yet, if anything I'm worse than before!
nodes.text: Nakon sastanka poslali su me na dodatnu krvnu pretragu za razinu testosterona, to je nešto novo za mene. Rekao sam osobi koja je uzimala krv da bude pažljiva s epruvetom jer bi uzorak mogao raznijeti uređaj ako nisu oprezni. Zasad nisam primijetio simptome niskog testosterona; ako išta, gori sam nego prije!

nodes.source: Have you noticed I don't mention the endless needle worries anymore, I have mentally got used to them and the sites used for taking blood from me have become immune to needle pricks. Either that or I haven't had a bad experience recently!!
nodes.text: Primjećujete li da više ne spominjem svoju beskrajnu brigu oko igala? Psihički sam se naviknuo na njih, a mjesta s kojih mi uzimaju krv gotovo su otupjela na ubode. Ili samo u posljednje vrijeme nisam imao loše iskustvo!!

nodes.source: 9th August 2005 - Tuesday
nodes.text: 9. kolovoza 2005. - utorak

nodes.source: 8 months since initial diagnosis today. It passed without me thinking of it at all, I rarely think of the diagnosis anniversaries anymore.
nodes.text: Danas je prošlo osam mjeseci od prve dijagnoze. Dan je prošao a da nisam ni pomislio na to. Na godišnjice dijagnoze gotovo više i ne mislim.

nodes.source: Talking of anniversaries I'm going to make it to another birthday very soon, on the 22nd August 2005 I will be another year older. In the past -like many of you out there I'm sure- I didn't like to think of getting another year older, but now at each birthday I'll be grateful I've been given the opportunity to live another year! Let's face it, luckily I'm a survivor and hopefully many, many more birthdays will now pass me by!
nodes.text: Kad smo već kod godišnjica, uskoro ću dočekati još jedan rođendan. Dana 22. kolovoza 2005. bit ću godinu dana stariji. Prije, kao i mnogi od vas, nisam volio pomisao da starim, ali sada ću na svaki rođendan biti zahvalan što mi je pružena prilika živjeti još jednu godinu! Srećom, preživio sam i nadam se da me čekaju još mnogi, mnogi rođendani!

nodes.source: Strangely, on this day today, fell a talk on Testicular Cancer at an Army base not too far from where I live. Given by the inimitable checkemlads.com crew, Mick Riley and Phil Morris (new pictures in my gallery) to a large audience of first year recruits, a perfect target audience. I was introduced and applauded for all that I had been through, something I'm sure no soldier however 'hard' would like to confront.
nodes.text: Zanimljivo, baš danas održano je predavanje o raku testisa u vojnoj bazi nedaleko od mjesta gdje živim. Održala ga je neponovljiva ekipa checkemlads.com, Mick Riley i Phil Morris (nove slike u galeriji), pred velikom publikom novaka prve godine, idealnom ciljnom skupinom. Predstavili su me i publika mi je zapljeskala zbog svega što sam prošao, nečega s čime se, siguran sam, ni najtvrđi vojnik ne bi želio suočiti.

nodes.source: I've also committed myself to a tandem sky dive with an Army team, on the 2nd of September 2005 with Mick and hopefully Phil. Jumping out of a plane at 13,000 feet was not something I had in mind to do in my life, but now I jump at every opportunity given to me (pardon the pun).
nodes.text: Također sam se obvezao na tandemski skok padobranom s vojnom ekipom 2. rujna 2005., zajedno s Mickom i nadam se Philom. Iskakanje iz aviona s 13.000 stopa nije bilo nešto što sam planirao u životu, ali sada skačem na svaku priliku (oprostite na dosjetki).

nodes.source: 12th August 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 12. kolovoza 2005. - petak

nodes.source: Blood test day today, popped in to my local hospital for it. Again the department was a ghost town, I caught the nurse in charge and was soon given my test.
nodes.text: Danas je dan za krvnu pretragu, pa sam svratio u lokalnu bolnicu. Odjel je opet bio pust kao grad duhova. Pronašao sam glavnu sestru i brzo obavio pretragu.

nodes.source: Each time I go along to these tests at another hospital I have a special letter and dispatch sticker to hand over. This makes sure that my blood tubes reach the right place.
nodes.text: Svaki put kada idem na ove pretrage u drugu bolnicu moram predati posebno pismo i naljepnicu za slanje uzorka. To osigurava da epruvete s mojom krvlju stignu na pravo mjesto.

nodes.source: Only 10 days to go and I'll make it to being another year older!
nodes.text: Još samo deset dana i dočekat ću još jednu godinu života!

nodes.source: 26th August 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 26. kolovoza 2005. - petak

nodes.source: Blood test day today, popped in to my local hospital for it. This time the department was full with people. I had to wait an hour before I was seen and tested, even then the nurse (a REED temp) did not know what to do with my paperwork, I had to explain how to take my blood, how much to take and what to do with the letter and sticker that I had brought for him.
nodes.text: Danas opet krvna pretraga u lokalnoj bolnici. Ovoga je puta odjel bio pun ljudi. Čekao sam sat vremena prije nego što sam došao na red, a tada sestra (privremeno zaposlena preko agencije REED) nije znala što s mojim papirima. Morao sam joj objasniti kako uzeti krv, koliko i što učiniti s pismom i naljepnicom koje sam donio.

nodes.source: Quite easily the worst experience of a blood test I have had to date, short of dragging me around the room whilst holding a needle which was stuck in my arm, the test was very uncomfortable indeed and it took 2 attempts at getting anything out of me. I was glad to get out of there! Still suffering with a few of those lasting Chemotherapy symptoms, which could possibly go on for a long time to come.
nodes.text: Bez sumnje najgore iskustvo vađenja krvi dosad. Jedino bi gore bilo da me vuku po prostoriji dok mi je igla zabodena u ruku! Bilo je vrlo neugodno i trebala su dva pokušaja da izvuku krv. Jedva sam čekao otići! I dalje imam nekoliko dugotrajnih simptoma nakon kemoterapije koji bi mogli trajati još dugo.

nodes.text: (još je prisutno, trebalo bi s vremenom nestati)

nodes.source: Lung twinges/pains
nodes.text: Probadajuća bol u plućima

nodes.source: (occasional) I have noticed that on the day after having had a few too many alcoholic beverages, the above symptoms are far more apparent. Think I'll go steady on the juice for a while!
nodes.text: (povremeno) Primijetio sam da su dan nakon nekoliko čašica previše gore navedeni simptomi mnogo izraženiji. Mislim da ću se neko vrijeme držati podalje od alkohola!

nodes.source: My birthday passed relatively quietly, I had many well wishers and a few cards/presents to boot. All in all and in my case especially I suppose I kind of hoped for a big surprise on the auspicious day, making it another year alive was most certainly the celebration. Perhaps I'll have to pull my finger out and organise my 'Ball'. Still, I'm running hard away from a 6-8 month hole in my finances, which is catching up with me and hurting bad.
nodes.text: Rođendan je prošao prilično mirno. Dobio sam mnogo lijepih želja, čestitki i nekoliko poklona. Sve u svemu, osobito u mojem slučaju, mislim da sam se potajno nadao velikom iznenađenju na taj važan dan, ali već je sama činjenica da sam preživio još jednu godinu bila razlog za slavlje. Možda se napokon moram trgnuti i organizirati svoju „loptu”. Ipak, još uvijek nastojim pobjeći od financijske rupe nastale zbog šest do osam mjeseci bez rada, koja me sada sustiže i poprilično boli.

nodes.source: Life afterwards
nodes.text: Život nakon liječenja

nodes.source: 14 February 2025
nodes.text: 14. veljače 2025.

nodes.source: Looking back at Charing Cross Hospital
nodes.text: Osvrt na bolnicu Charing Cross

nodes.source: Charing Cross Hospital, 14 February 2025. My last visit before discharge from follow-up care.
nodes.text: Bolnica Charing Cross, 14. veljače 2025. Moj posljednji posjet prije otpusta iz dugotrajnog praćenja.

nodes.source: Some of you might remember this chapter of my life… 20 years ago, I walked out of this hospital after completing some gruelling chemotherapy treatment for Stage IIIb Testicular Cancer. I didn’t know what the future held or if I’d make it another 20 years - but I hoped.
nodes.text: Neki od vas možda se sjećaju ovog poglavlja mojeg života... Prije dvadeset godina izašao sam iz ove bolnice nakon iscrpljujuće kemoterapije zbog raka testisa stadija IIIb. Nisam znao što me čeka ni hoću li doživjeti još dvadeset godina, ali nadao sam se.

nodes.source: Recently, of all days, on Valentine’s Day, I walked out of those same doors for the last time. I paused, feeling a little emotional, looked back and took this picture.
nodes.text: Nedavno, baš na Valentinovo, posljednji sam put izašao kroz ta ista vrata. Zastao sam, pomalo ganut, osvrnuo se i snimio ovu fotografiju.

nodes.source: Life is a gift, and sometimes the hardest journeys lead to the most meaningful milestones. Here’s to the next 20 years and whatever lies ahead! x
nodes.text: Život je dar, a ponekad nas najteži putovi dovedu do najvažnijih prekretnica. Za sljedećih dvadeset godina i sve što nas čeka! x

nodes.source: On 14 February 2025, I was discharged from the care of Charing Cross Hospital, twenty years after my original treatment. My HCG results continued to be below 2 (normal) at my annual February follow-ups.
nodes.text: Dana 14. veljače 2025. otpušten sam iz skrbi bolnice Charing Cross, dvadeset godina nakon prvog liječenja. Nalazi HCG-a ostali su ispod dva, odnosno u granicama normale, na godišnjim kontrolama u veljači.

nodes.source: See the HCG follow-up results
nodes.text: Pogledajte kontrolne nalaze HCG-a

nodes.source: January 2015
nodes.text: Siječanj 2015.

nodes.source: Very nearly 10 years clear.
nodes.text: Gotovo deset godina bez raka.

nodes.source: So I'm about to reach the 10 year clear milestone, but with the saddest news.
nodes.text: Upravo se približavam desetoj godišnjici bez znakova raka, ali uz najtužnije vijesti.

nodes.source: After my enduring experience with Cancer and brush with the edge of life itself, my precious and beautiful daughter, who is almost 4 years old, has just been diagnosed with a brain tumour. She's just about to undergo many years of chemotherapy, radiotherapy and proton beam therapy.
nodes.text: Nakon svega što sam prošao s rakom i dodira sa samim rubom života, mojoj dragocjenoj i prekrasnoj kćeri, koja uskoro puni četiri godine, upravo je dijagnosticiran tumor mozga. Pred njom su godine kemoterapije, radioterapije i liječenja protonskim snopom.

nodes.source: This is totally unrelated and in no way connected to my illness (genetically or otherwise), just complete and utter rotten luck. In fact I am finding it extremely hard to believe both mine and my partners luck, and of course that of my daughter. Who's child deserves such rotten luck? I have no words to describe how devastated we are. I can honestly say I would happily go through my illness all over again to take this away from my precious little girl.
nodes.text: To je potpuno nepovezano s mojom bolešću, genetski ili na bilo koji drugi način. Jednostavno nevjerojatno loša sreća. Zaista mi je teško vjerovati kakva je nesreća zadesila mene, moju partnericu i, naravno, našu kćer. Čije dijete zaslužuje takvu nesreću? Nemam riječi za to koliko smo shrvani. Iskreno, rado bih sve svoje liječenje prošao ponovno kad bih time mogao poštedjeti svoju dragocjenu djevojčicu.

nodes.source: You can follow her story from her website and on twitter at: www.eleanorstollery.com
nodes.text: Njezinu priču možete pratiti na web-stranici i Twitteru: www.eleanorstollery.com

nodes.source: Below in chronological order...
nodes.text: U nastavku, kronološkim redom...

nodes.source: September 2005 1st September 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: Rujan 2005. - 1. rujna 2005., petak

nodes.source: Routine blood tests, X-Ray and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danas rutinske krvne pretrage, rendgenska snimka i susret s konzultantom u bolnici Charing Cross.

nodes.source: Battled with the usual bad traffic in to London today, which meant I was slightly late for the meeting with my Consultant. Once I'd arrived and the blood tests were carried out, my Consultant had gone to an important meeting so I was seen by his Registrar instead.
nodes.text: Opet sam se borio s uobičajenom prometnom gužvom prema Londonu i malo zakasnio na sastanak. Kad sam stigao i dao krv, moj je konzultant otišao na važan sastanak pa me primio specijalizant.

nodes.source: I was soon sent for an X-Ray and came back to the Registrar for the results. All good. After a brief chat and confirmation of my next check-up date I left the hospital.
nodes.text: Ubrzo su me poslali na rendgen, a zatim sam se vratio specijalizantu po nalaz. Sve je dobro. Nakon kratkog razgovora i potvrde sljedeće kontrole otišao sam iz bolnice.

nodes.source: 27th September 2005 - Tuesday
nodes.text: 27. rujna 2005. - utorak

nodes.source: Blood test day today, popped in to my local hospital for it. Again the department was quite busy. I had to wait an hour before I was seen and tested.
nodes.text: Danas sam svratio u mjesnu bolnicu na vađenje krvi. Odjel je opet bio prilično zauzet. Čekao sam sat vremena prije nego što su me primili.

nodes.source: My favourite vein isn't working too well anymore! It's gone a bit hard. Guess I'll have to find another good one which gives limited pain, whilst the other recovers!
nodes.text: Moja omiljena vena više ne radi baš dobro! Postala je pomalo tvrda. Morat ću pronaći drugu dobru venu koja ne boli previše dok se ova oporavlja!

nodes.source: The blood test only takes a maximum of 5 minutes and I was soon released with a couple of attempt holes covered by cotton wool and tape!
nodes.text: Samo vađenje traje najviše pet minuta i ubrzo sam pušten s nekoliko rupica od pokušaja, pokrivenih vatom i flasterom!

nodes.source: I've got some more questions for my consultant to answer. Hopefully on my next visit to Charing Cross Hospital I'll get to see him. See you back here on the 7th October.
nodes.text: Imam još pitanja za konzultanta. Nadam se da ću ga vidjeti na sljedećem posjetu Charing Crossu. Vidimo se ovdje 7. listopada.

nodes.source: October 2005 7th October 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: Listopad 2005. - 7. listopada 2005., petak

nodes.source: Routine blood tests and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danas rutinske krvne pretrage i susret s konzultantom u bolnici Charing Cross.

nodes.source: I had made a late appointment with my Consultant today as the plan was to go for a bite to eat with him after my routine check-up in order to discuss a web-site he would like me to look at developing.
nodes.text: Dogovorio sam kasniji termin s konzultantom jer je plan bio da nakon rutinske kontrole zajedno nešto pojedemo i razgovaramo o web-stranici koju bi želio da mu razvijem.

nodes.source: During my 'check-up' conversations with my Consultant I always try to give a very good indication as to how I have been feeling since we last spoke and any symptoms that I might still have or have developed.
nodes.text: Tijekom kontrolnih razgovora s konzultantom uvijek nastojim što točnije opisati kako sam se osjećao od prošlog susreta i koje simptome još imam ili sam ih u međuvremenu razvio.

nodes.source: One symptom recently has been a few mild but odd headaches in the left side of my head, my Consultant didn't seem too concerned as my treatment has been very successful and consequent blood tests/scans have shown no signs of any new activity whatsoever, nonetheless he booked me in for a low priority MRI scan on my head!
nodes.text: Nedavno sam imao nekoliko blagih, ali čudnih glavobolja s lijeve strane glave. Konzultant nije djelovao zabrinuto jer je liječenje bilo vrlo uspješno, a kasniji nalazi i snimke ne pokazuju nikakve znakove nove aktivnosti. Ipak me naručio na MR glave, bez žurnosti!

nodes.source: My body has been through quite a battle over the past year, I would like to -try to- think that any or all of the pains I get from time to time, sometimes daily, are just part of recovery or even old age! As my Consultant once said to me, "each and every new pain I get from now on will come as a renewed and far more heightened worry to me". The likelihood of it being anything as sinister as before is pretty slim especially as time goes on.
nodes.text: Moje je tijelo tijekom protekle godine prošlo veliku bitku. Volio bih vjerovati da su svi povremeni, katkad svakodnevni bolovi samo dio oporavka ili čak starenja! Kako mi je konzultant jednom rekao: 'Svaka nova bol koju odsad osjetim izazvat će u meni obnovljenu i mnogo snažniju zabrinutost.' Vjerojatnost da je riječ o nečem tako zlokobnom kao prije vrlo je mala, osobito kako vrijeme prolazi.

nodes.source: I have heard Cancer called the silent killer before, now I know what that really means. However, there are many positives I can turn to, one of which being that I am regularly checked up on at the hospital, so I must not ponder on what could be and just get on with my life, a plentiful one with a new perspective!
nodes.text: Već sam čuo da rak zovu tihim ubojicom, a sada znam što to zaista znači. Ipak, mnogo je pozitivnih stvari, među njima i činjenica da me u bolnici redovito kontroliraju. Zato ne smijem stalno razmišljati što bi moglo biti, nego nastaviti živjeti punim životom, s novim pogledom na njega!

nodes.source: I have to remind myself before going out for a few too many drinks that the day after brings on the above symptoms much more! No sympathy expected there!
nodes.text: Prije nego što izađem popiti koju čašu previše, moram se podsjetiti da su svi navedeni simptomi sljedeći dan znatno jači! Tu ne očekujem suosjećanje!

nodes.source: I managed to grab a business related chat with my Consultant following my check-up and hopefully will be working with him on a revised and informative web-site related to a very rare Cancer. I will of course post the link when it's launched!
nodes.text: Nakon kontrole uspio sam s konzultantom popričati i o poslu. Nadam se da ćemo zajedno raditi na novoj, informativnoj web-stranici o vrlo rijetkom obliku raka. Naravno, objavit ću poveznicu kad bude dostupna!

nodes.source: A few days back I went to lunch with my good friend and fellow survivor Milton Mermikides someone I'm sure you are familiar with if you have followed my story or are a recent reader of the entire story! We sat in a restaurant in a totally normal environment eating totally normal food, a surreal experience for us both after what we have been through. I hadn't seen Milton for sometime and he's looking really well as I think I am too (compared to what we both looked like in hospital anyway), in fact we hadn't known anything different of each other! Both Milton and I felt like shouting from the rooftops the elation we felt about being back in the normal world doing normal things and feeling normal again! Something which to external perception no one would have any idea of, we were just two blokes sitting in a restaurant eating!
nodes.text: Prije nekoliko dana ručao sam sa svojim dobrim prijateljem i kolegom koji je preživio rak, Miltonom Mermikidesom. Sigurno ga poznajete ako pratite moju priču ili ste nedavno pročitali cijelu! Sjedili smo u restoranu, u posve normalnom okruženju, i jeli posve normalnu hranu. Nakon svega što smo prošli obojici nam je to bilo gotovo nestvarno iskustvo. Miltona nisam vidio neko vrijeme i izgleda stvarno dobro, a mislim da i ja izgledam tako, barem u usporedbi s našim izgledom u bolnici. Zapravo nikad nismo ni vidjeli jedan drugoga u drukčijem stanju! Obojica smo poželjela vikati s krovova koliko smo sretni što smo se vratili u normalan svijet, radimo normalne stvari i opet se osjećamo normalno! A nitko sa strane ne bi imao pojma. Bili smo samo dvojica muškaraca koji sjede u restoranu i jedu!

nodes.source: November 2005 4th November 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: Studeni 2005. - 4. studenoga 2005., petak

nodes.source: Routine blood tests, X-Ray and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danas rutinske krvne pretrage, rendgenska snimka i susret s konzultantom u bolnici Charing Cross.

nodes.source: Breezed in to Charing Cross, no traffic today.
nodes.text: Bez problema sam stigao u Charing Cross, danas nije bilo gužve.

nodes.source: Saw my friendly Phlebotomists, I mentioned to them that they have now known me almost a year, as on the 10th December it will be 1 year since I was first at Charing Cross Hospital. Doesn't time fly when you're having fun!
nodes.text: Vidio sam svoje ljubazne djelatnike koji mi vade krv. Spomenuo sam im da me poznaju već gotovo godinu dana jer će 10. prosinca biti točno godinu dana od mojeg prvog dolaska u Charing Cross. Kako vrijeme leti kad se dobro zabavljate!

nodes.source: I was soon seen by my Consultant. Not much to say today really, I collected some up to date printouts of blood results, had my physical examination and collected my X-Ray form. He wasn't happy with how the 'NHS system' had allocated a date for my MRI head scan, so this may now be prioritised a little higher and brought forward to as early as November or December 2005.
nodes.text: Konzultant me ubrzo primio. Danas zapravo nema mnogo novosti. Uzeo sam nove ispise krvnih nalaza, obavio tjelesni pregled i dobio uputnicu za rendgen. Nije bio zadovoljan načinom na koji mi je sustav NHS-a odredio termin MR-a glave, pa bi pregled mogao dobiti viši prioritet i biti pomaknut već na studeni ili prosinac 2005.

nodes.source: Other than that he is very happy with my progress, the treatment has been very effective and I am well and truly on my way to making it back to 100%25 health - my blood results over the past few tests show that I am still just out of the normal ranges. It takes approximately 1 year for the effects of BEP Chemotherapy to fully dissipate from the human body, in some cases longer.
nodes.text: Inače je vrlo zadovoljan mojim napretkom. Liječenje je bilo vrlo učinkovito i ozbiljno sam na putu prema stopostotnom zdravlju. Posljednjih nekoliko krvnih nalaza pokazuje da su mi neke vrijednosti još malo izvan normale. Učincima BEP kemoterapije treba približno godinu dana da posve nestanu iz ljudskog tijela, a katkad i dulje.

nodes.source: Bumped in to a fellow patient in the waiting room, I met him along with his parents some time back during my treatment days in hospital and he is still battling hard it seems. I can only wish him and his family well in the face of Cancer which I am sure Charing Cross is doing everything it can to defeat.
nodes.text: U čekaonici sam susreo jednog pacijenta kojeg sam s roditeljima upoznao tijekom liječenja. Čini se da se još snažno bori. Mogu samo njemu i njegovoj obitelji poželjeti sve najbolje u borbi protiv raka, za čije izlječenje sam siguran da Charing Cross čini sve što može.

nodes.source: Off for my X-Ray, as usual a quick and painless experience with what looked to my eye like a good result (the Radiographer kindly showed me the resulting scan), however it takes a few days for a Radiologist to check it out properly.
nodes.text: Zatim na rendgen, kao obično brzo i bezbolno iskustvo. Snimka je mojim očima izgledala dobro, radiološki tehnolog ljubazno mi ju je pokazao, ali radiolog je mora pravilno pregledati tijekom sljedećih dana.

nodes.source: Once again I was free to leave the hospital, back in to the open world and on with my life. See you again on the 2nd December 2005.
nodes.text: Još jednom sam mogao slobodno izaći iz bolnice u otvoreni svijet i nastaviti sa životom. Vidimo se ponovno 2. prosinca 2005.

nodes.source: December 2005
nodes.text: Prosinac 2005.

nodes.source: 2nd December 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 2. prosinca 2005. - petak

nodes.source: Routine blood tests and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danas rutinske krvne pretrage i susret s konzultantom u bolnici Charing Cross.

nodes.source: Arrived behind time today, been rushed off my feet this week what with arriving back from abroad later than I expected.
nodes.text: Danas sam zakasnio jer sam ovaj tjedan bio zatrpan obvezama, a iz inozemstva sam se vratio kasnije nego što sam očekivao.

nodes.source: Blood tests carried out very quickly, I pretty much walked straight in and before I knew it I had given 4 test tubes of blood. One and most importantly for my tumour markers (HCG), two to monitor my general health (U&E's & FBC) and finally one for my testosterone levels.
nodes.text: Krv su mi uzeli vrlo brzo. Praktički sam samo ušao i već su napunili četiri epruvete: jednu, najvažniju, za tumorske biljege HCG; dvije za opće zdravlje, ureju, elektrolite i kompletnu krvnu sliku; te posljednju za testosteron.

nodes.source: Had to wait for my Consultant for a bit which was totally understandable as Clinic had all but closed for business and he had left to continue with his work elsewhere. Clinic reception kindly called him to see if he was free to come back for me.
nodes.text: Morao sam malo pričekati konzultanta, što je bilo razumljivo jer se ambulanta gotovo zatvorila i on je već otišao nastaviti posao drugdje. Ljubazna recepcija nazvala ga je i pitala može li se vratiti zbog mene.

nodes.source: Everything still looking good as far as my recovery is concerned, testosterone levels are within UK normal ranges, last months X-Ray results have been studied and the -some would say, rather awkward- physical examination checked out all fine.
nodes.text: Što se oporavka tiče, sve i dalje izgleda dobro. Testosteron je u britanskim referentnim granicama, proučeni su prošlomjesečni rendgenski nalazi, a i tjelesni pregled, koji bi neki nazvali pomalo nezgodnim, prošao je bez problema.

nodes.source: Comments on last months X-Ray even stated that there is now little or no evidence of any damage in my lungs, something I am astounded by. A CT scan would most likely show up some scarring, but there is no need for a CT at this stage.
nodes.text: U komentaru na prošlomjesečnu snimku čak stoji da sada gotovo nema znakova oštećenja u mojim plućima, što me zapanjilo. CT bi vjerojatno pokazao poneki ožiljak, ali trenutačno za njega nema potrebe.

nodes.source: Certainly all signs of a fine recovery in progress.
nodes.text: Sve su to znakovi da oporavak odlično napreduje.

nodes.source: My MRI scan has now been brought forward to the 19th December 2005 and my next routine check-up is scheduled slightly earlier on the 23rd December 2005, as I will be away when it is actually due around the beginning of the new year.
nodes.text: MR je sada pomaknut na 19. prosinca 2005., a sljedeća rutinska kontrola nešto ranije, na 23. prosinca, jer ću biti odsutan kad bi inače trebala biti početkom nove godine.

nodes.source: I'll put pen to paper (or keys to the web!) on my first diagnosis anniversary which is fast approaching on the 9th December 2005. I will not be celebrating as I don't think celebrating the diagnosis of a life threatening illness is very apt.
nodes.text: Ponovno ću se prihvatiti pisanja (odnosno tipkanja za web!) na prvu godišnjicu dijagnoze, koja se brzo približava, 9. prosinca 2005. Neću slaviti jer mi se proslava godišnjice dijagnoze bolesti opasne po život ne čini prikladnom.

nodes.source: 9th December 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 9. prosinca 2005. - petak

nodes.source: The 9th of December 2005 passed relatively quietly for me and was certainly a day I choose to reflect on the year that has passed. Although it's been tough at times, I'm most certainly glad to still be here and to have out lived the "less than a year to live" statement.
nodes.text: Deveti prosinca prošao je za mene prilično mirno. Bio je to dan kad sam odlučio razmisliti o godini iza sebe. Iako je katkad bilo vrlo teško, neizmjerno mi je drago što sam još ovdje i što sam nadživio prognozu 'manje od godinu dana života'.

nodes.source: This website has been a great help to me, as an outlet for my thoughts and fears during my treatment, surgery and ongoing recovery. It now stands as a testament, a message of strength and positivity to others. Others not only suffering with a similar illness or disease to mine, but for anybody who faces a challenge of such enormity in relation to life's twists and turns. You can win through, you have to just keep on going, keep looking forwards and stay positive. I did and look where it got me, still here and living life to the full.
nodes.text: Ova web-stranica mnogo mi je pomogla kao mjesto na kojem sam tijekom liječenja, operacije i oporavka mogao izraziti misli i strahove. Sada je svjedočanstvo i poruka snage i optimizma drugima. Ne samo ljudima koji boluju od slične bolesti nego svima pred kojima stoji ogroman izazov usred životnih preokreta. Možete uspjeti, samo nastavite ići naprijed, gledati prema budućnosti i ostati pozitivni. Ja jesam, i pogledajte kamo me to dovelo: još sam ovdje i živim punim plućima.

nodes.source: Not many people remembered or reminded me of this day just a few close friends. I made a note of it in my diary, although I doubt I'll ever be able to forget what happened a year ago today, I have the scars to remind me forever.
nodes.text: Nije mnogo ljudi zapamtilo ovaj datum ili me na njega podsjetilo, samo nekoliko bliskih prijatelja. Zabilježio sam ga u dnevnik, iako sumnjam da ću ikada zaboraviti što se dogodilo prije točno godinu dana. Ožiljci će me na to podsjećati zauvijek.

nodes.source: Has it changed me? Well, I have certainly been given the opportunity to see life with a different perspective completely, a gift if you like or simply a second chance in the face of death. At no point before in my life before this happened would I stop to think that a certain day would be the last day of its kind in my life, ONE LIFE, so as the 9th of December 2005 passes I will never see another day the same in my life. There is no ground hog day. So we only get one shot of this existence, make the most you possibly can of it.
nodes.text: Je li me to promijenilo? Pa, svakako sam dobio priliku gledati život iz sasvim drukčije perspektive, kao dar ili drugu priliku pred licem smrti. Nikad prije ovoga nisam zastao i pomislio da je neki određeni dan posljednji takav dan mojeg života. IMAMO SAMO JEDAN ŽIVOT. Kad prođe 9. prosinca 2005., nikad više neću doživjeti isti takav dan. Nema beskrajnog ponavljanja istog dana. Dakle, imamo samo jednu priliku za ovo postojanje i trebamo je iskoristiti najbolje što možemo.

nodes.source: What are you going to do today and with the rest of your life?
nodes.text: Što ćete napraviti danas i s ostatkom svojeg života?

nodes.source: You never know what life has in store for you, what's around the next corner... this disease crept up through my body for over a year and a half, practically unbeknown to me, scary isn't it!
nodes.text: Nikad ne znate što vam život sprema, što se krije iza sljedećeg ugla... Ova se bolest više od godinu i pol gotovo neprimjetno širila mojim tijelom, a ja nisam imao pojma. Zastrašujuće, zar ne!

nodes.source: People ask me if I am 'cured' or 'recovered'. My understanding of being 'cured' of Cancer is there is NO cure, if you survive it and the treatment, you live in remission of the disease for the rest of your life, your body has shown the potential for Cancer so your chances are slightly higher than most (of it coming back), however there are many other health statistics that will beat this in to a minute possibility.
nodes.text: Ljudi me pitaju jesam li 'izliječen' ili 'oporavljen'. Kako sam tada razumio pojam 'izliječen od raka', mislio sam da nema potpunog jamstva: ako preživite bolest i liječenje, živite u remisiji do kraja života. Vaše je tijelo pokazalo sklonost razvoju raka, pa je rizik od povratka nešto veći. Ipak, mnoge druge zdravstvene opasnosti statistički su vjerojatnije.

nodes.source: Am I fully recovered? NO, I am still very tired; my body is recovering from the effects of chemotherapy, which will take sometime. Although to all external appearances I might appear fit and healthy, I just do not have the stamina or the tenacity I did before. It will come with time.
nodes.text: Jesam li se potpuno oporavio? NE. Još sam jako umoran. Tijelo se oporavlja od kemoterapije i trebat će mu vremena. Iako izvana možda izgledam zdravo i snažno, nemam izdržljivost i upornost kao prije. To će se s vremenom vratiti.

nodes.source: All this affects my work and my finances substantially enough to reverberate for a long time to come. There is no possible way you can imagine that you would have to plan financially for a major illness in your life, you just don't think it will happen to you.
nodes.text: Sve to znatno utječe na moj posao i financije, s posljedicama koje će se osjećati još dugo. Nikad ne pomislite da biste trebali financijski planirati tešku bolest u vlastitom životu. Jednostavno ne mislite da će se dogoditi vama.

nodes.source: This Christmas should certainly be a better one; at least I'm not going to be eating a hospital Christmas dinner attached to a Chemotherapy IV drip!
nodes.text: Ovogodišnji Božić sigurno će biti bolji. Barem neću jesti bolnički božićni ručak priključen na infuziju kemoterapije!

nodes.source: I'm not sure how many of you out there still follow my story and have done so from its inception back in mid December 2004. It's been a long year for me, a life changing experience, how has yours passed?
nodes.text: Ne znam koliko vas još prati moju priču od njezina početka sredinom prosinca 2004. Bila je to duga godina i iskustvo koje mi je promijenilo život. Kako je prošla vaša?

nodes.source: 19th December 2005 - Monday
nodes.text: 19. prosinca 2005. - ponedjeljak

nodes.source: Arrived early for my MRI appointment. The MRI department is normally a pretty busy place so I was kept waiting about 45 minutes for my scan.
nodes.text: Stigao sam rano na MR. Odjel za magnetsku rezonanciju obično je vrlo zauzet pa sam čekao snimanje oko 45 minuta.

nodes.source: Usual procedure, remove all metals, credit cards and pretty much everything from my person apart from my clothes. You are given a little locker to store it all in.
nodes.text: Uobičajeni postupak: ukloniti sve metalno, kreditne kartice i praktički sve sa sebe osim odjeće. Za to dobijete mali ormarić.

nodes.source: Once in the scanner it takes about 30-45 minutes in total to complete an MRI brain scan, half way through there is an injection of a special colourant to further highlight areas of the brain.
nodes.text: Kad uđete u uređaj, MR mozga traje ukupno otprilike 30 do 45 minuta. Na polovici pregleda ubrizgavaju posebno kontrastno sredstvo koje dodatno ističe dijelove mozga.

nodes.source: Whenever I go for these 'scans', be it X-Rays, CT's or MRI's I always try to judge the operators reaction once its complete, after all, I was fairly accurate in my judgement of the radiologists reaction to my first ever X-Ray over a year ago!
nodes.text: Kad god idem na snimanja, bila to rendgenska, CT ili MR, uvijek pokušavam procijeniti reakciju osoblja na kraju. Uostalom, prije više od godinu dana prilično sam točno procijenio reakciju radiologa na moju prvu rendgensku snimku!

nodes.source: 23rd December 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 23. prosinca 2005. - petak

nodes.source: I was quite late for my appointment today and I paid for it (not intentionally I might add). Today's blood test was a painful one, the blood was taken from a not often used vein. The sister was chatting to me whilst the test was underway so my mind was taken off of the pain somewhat, still, I hate it when it hurts like that.
nodes.text: Danas sam dosta zakasnio na termin i zbog toga platio cijenu, nenamjerno, naravno. Vađenje krvi bilo je bolno jer su je uzeli iz vene koju rijetko koriste. Glavna sestra razgovarala je sa mnom tijekom postupka pa mi je malo odvukla pozornost s boli. Ipak, mrzim kad tako boli.

nodes.source: My Consultant was called back from his staff Christmas lunch break which had almost begun (sorry!), just to speak with me. This was my last meeting with him before I was due to go abroad for a considerable length of time, a first since I had been ill.
nodes.text: Pozvali su mojeg konzultanta natrag s božićnog ručka osoblja, koji je već gotovo počeo, samo da razgovara sa mnom. Oprostite! Bio je to naš posljednji susret prije mojeg duljeg putovanja u inozemstvo, prvog otkako sam se razbolio.

nodes.source: Everything checked out fine. Results from my previous tests were discussed. Nothing showed up on the MRI, bloods returning to normal values, all looking good so far. I am in the very high 90's in terms of percentage for making a complete return to normal health. I was given an X-Ray form as it was X-Ray time again and an appointment for almost immediately after I was due to return from my trip.
nodes.text: Sve je bilo u redu. Razgovarali smo o prethodnim nalazima. MR nije pokazao ništa zabrinjavajuće, krvne vrijednosti vraćaju se u normalu i zasad sve izgleda dobro. Izgledi za potpuni povratak zdravlju iznose više od 90 posto, blizu sam stopostotnom oporavku. Dobio sam uputnicu za rendgen jer je opet došlo vrijeme za snimanje i termin kontrole gotovo odmah nakon povratka s putovanja.

nodes.source: Once at the X-Ray department I had quite a wait to be seen. I normally take most of the day out to do a hospital visit so this didn't concern me too much and after all my welfare is what is most important to me otherwise I would be no good to anyone. X-Ray done and I was free to go.
nodes.text: Na rendgenskom odjelu opet sam dosta čekao. Za posjet bolnici obično odvojim veći dio dana pa me to nije previše brinulo. Naposljetku, zdravlje mi je najvažnije, bez njega ne bih koristio nikome. Snimanje je završilo i mogao sam otići.

nodes.source: January 2006
nodes.text: siječanj 2006.

nodes.source: 27th January 2006 - Friday
nodes.text: 27. siječnja 2006. - petak

nodes.source: Back from abroad. I was quite ill whilst away, towards the end of my trip, probably the illest I've been since treatment. It's a scary place to be when you're over 4000 miles away from your home comforts. I was glad to have been given the opportunity to get away for a well deserved break but at the same time I was glad to be back within my comfort zone.
nodes.text: Vratio sam se iz inozemstva. Pred kraj putovanja bio sam prilično bolestan, vjerojatno najteže otkako je liječenje završilo. Zastrašujuće je kad ste više od 6400 kilometara daleko od udobnosti svojeg doma. Bilo mi je drago što sam napokon imao priliku otići na zasluženi odmor, ali isto tako i vratiti se u poznato okruženje.

nodes.source: Routine blood tests and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danas rutinske krvne pretrage i susret s konzultantom u bolnici Charing Cross.

nodes.source: Good and relatively painless blood test (I like it when it goes smoothly). If you ever wondered what goes on at a blood test have a look at Milton's recent video here, this is something we have both become pretty much accustomed to over time!
nodes.text: Vađenje krvi bilo je dobro i prilično bezbolno, volim kad sve ide glatko. Ako ste se ikad pitali kako to izgleda, pogledajte Miltonov nedavni video. Na takve smo se postupke obojica s vremenom gotovo posve naviknuli!

nodes.source: Was swiftly seen by my Consultant, again everything in order, physical examination out of the way and off I go!
nodes.text: Konzultant me brzo primio. Ponovno je sve bilo u redu, obavili smo tjelesni pregled i mogao sam otići!

nodes.source: My next appointment will be the last of my monthly check-ups, after which it goes to every 2 months with X-Rays on alternative visits as before.
nodes.text: Sljedeća kontrola bit će posljednja mjesečna. Nakon toga dolazit ću svaka dva mjeseca, uz rendgenska snimanja pri svakom drugom posjetu kao i dosad.

nodes.source: February 2006
nodes.text: Veljača 2006.

nodes.source: 8th February 2006 - Wednesday
nodes.text: 8. veljače 2006. - srijeda

nodes.source: A mental note... ONE YEAR CLEAR OF CANCER IN MY BLOOD!
nodes.text: Bilješka za sebe... GODINU DANA BEZ ZNAKOVA RAKA U KRVI!

nodes.source: Did anybody really notice, not a chance, "life goes on", something to always remember!
nodes.text: Je li to itko primijetio? Naravno da nije. 'Život ide dalje.' To treba uvijek imati na umu!

nodes.source: 24th February 2006 - Friday
nodes.text: 24. veljače 2006. - petak

nodes.source: My first official blood test since my landmark one year clear date. Today's test will eventually confirm 'officially' if I am to make the one year of untraceable HCG markers in my blood. The chances of my Testicular Cancer coming back are diminishing as time goes by and passing the one year mark just makes it all look that much better!
nodes.text: Moje prvo službeno vađenje krvi nakon važne godišnjice bez raka. Današnji nalaz konačno će 'službeno' potvrditi imam li punu godinu dana nemjerljivog HCG-a u krvi. Vjerojatnost povratka raka testisa s vremenom se smanjuje, a prelazak prve godine sve čini još obećavajućim!

nodes.source: Arrived at Hospital in a rush today. Got a lot of things going on in my life outside of hospital now, it's a comfort to come in and get checked up but sometimes feels like a chore. However, I wouldn't miss it for the world and my appointments can be made somewhat flexible if required. So despite the drag of driving to Charing Cross Hospital, it comes pretty high up on my agenda!
nodes.text: Danas sam u bolnicu stigao u žurbi. Sada mi se izvan bolnice mnogo toga događa i utješno je doći na kontrolu, premda katkad djeluje kao obveza. Ipak, nikad je ne bih propustio, a termini se po potrebi mogu malo prilagoditi. Unatoč napornoj vožnji do Charing Crossa, kontrola mi je visoko na listi prioriteta!

nodes.source: As soon as I walked through the door I was greeted by my friendly Phlebotomists. Another landmark today, I WATCHED for the first time, every detail, a big deal for me, but I was feeling strong so I went for it. The needle went in and I hardly felt a thing, 4 test tubes of blood taken (it amazes me how fast it spurts out!). One and most importantly for my tumour markers (HCG), two to monitor my general health (U&E's & FBC) and finally one for my testosterone levels.
nodes.text: Čim sam ušao, pozdravili su me ljubazni djelatnici koji mi uzimaju krv. Danas još jedna prekretnica: prvi sam put GLEDAO cijeli postupak, svaki detalj. Za mene je to velika stvar, ali osjećao sam se snažno pa sam odlučio pokušati. Igla je ušla, gotovo ništa nisam osjetio i uzeli su četiri epruvete. Nevjerojatno mi je kako brzo krv izlazi! Jedna je, najvažnija, za HCG, dvije za opće zdravlje, ureju, elektrolite i kompletnu krvnu sliku, a posljednja za testosteron.

nodes.source: Spoke with Dr. Savage who also seemed happy the year had so far been clear for me! I showed him some amazing new images I have had created from an old CT scan, you can see them in the 'Results' section of my site, of which he was suitably impressed (thanks go to Antoine Rosset of OsiriX fame) and the Apple Mac of course!
nodes.text: Razgovarao sam s dr. Savageom, koji je također bio sretan što je prošla godina bez znakova raka! Pokazao sam mu nevjerojatne nove slike koje su izrađene iz starog CT-a. Možete ih vidjeti u odjeljku 'Rezultati' na mojoj stranici. Primjereno je bio impresioniran, a zahvalnost ide Antoineu Rossetu, poznatom po OsiriXu, i naravno Apple Macu!

nodes.source: Got the all important physical examination out of the way, collected my X-Ray appointment form, arranged my next appointment and I was off.
nodes.text: Obavio sam najvažniji tjelesni pregled, preuzeo uputnicu za rendgen, dogovorio sljedeću kontrolu i krenuo kući.

nodes.source: Once at the X-Ray department, I had to wait a little while for it to be taken. My name was called and it was all done in seconds, had a quick peek and all looked good to me. I collected quite a crowd of radiographers around me as I showed off the CT imagery and as with every time I visit them and tell my story they are amazed and pleased at my progress from what they can see was quite a nasty spread.
nodes.text: Na rendgenskom odjelu morao sam malo pričekati. Prozvali su me i sve je bilo gotovo za nekoliko sekundi. Brzo sam bacio pogled i meni je sve izgledalo dobro. Oko mene se okupilo prilično mnogo radioloških tehnologa dok sam im pokazivao CT slike. Kao i svaki put kad im ispričam svoju priču, zadivljeni su i zadovoljni mojim napretkom nakon tako teškog širenja raka.

nodes.source: That was my last monthly check-up. I now move to every two months with chest X-Rays on alternate visits as before, obviously more spread out. A radiation break for my chest!
nodes.text: To je bila moja posljednja mjesečna kontrola. Sada dolazim svaka dva mjeseca, a rendgen pluća obavljat će se pri svakom drugom posjetu kao i prije, samo s većim razmacima. Malo predaha od zračenja za moja prsa!

nodes.source: I do hope this website is helping someone out there. Please feel free to email me to ask questions... don't be afraid.
nodes.text: Iskreno se nadam da ova stranica nekome pomaže. Slobodno mi pošaljite e-poruku s pitanjima... nemojte se bojati.

nodes.source: Unless anything changes, see you back here on April the 14th 2006, one year on from that scary operation (there will be new scar pictures)!
nodes.text: Ako se ništa ne promijeni, vidimo se ovdje 14. travnja 2006., godinu dana nakon one zastrašujuće operacije. Bit će i novih fotografija ožiljaka!

nodes.source: April 2006 14th April 2006 - Friday
nodes.text: Travanj 2006. - 14. travnja 2006., petak

nodes.source: One year on, since that daunting day.
nodes.text: Godinu dana nakon tog strašnog dana.

nodes.source: I remember it well, in retrospect I was totally distraught with worry, fear and anxiety. I could have filled buckets with the tears I shed. An operation that I was certainly not looking forward to.
nodes.text: Dobro ga pamtim. Kad se osvrnem, bio sam potpuno shrvan brigom, strahom i tjeskobom. Mogao sam napuniti kante suzama koje sam isplakao. Bila je to operacija kojoj se nipošto nisam radovao.

nodes.source: I went through a lot, although at the time it's happening to you it seems that you just have to get on with things and take each day as it comes. Dealing with the unknown seems easier in comparison. Looking back at the whole thing, it was massive and I'm very lucky to be here writing this!
nodes.text: Prošao sam mnogo toga, ali dok se sve događa, čini vam se da jednostavno morate nastaviti i prihvaćati svaki dan kako dolazi. Nositi se s nepoznatim tad se čak čini lakšim. Kad pogledam unatrag, sve je bilo golemo i vrlo sam sretan što sam ovdje i mogu ovo pisati!

nodes.source: Having friends and family around me, supporting me was a blessing. Reading through the 14th April 2005's diary entry really touches me. It took a fair chunk out of my life to overcome the Cancer, which the effects of, particularly financial, are still with me. My body has been through a lot, only time will tell if I am to get rid of some of the lasting symptoms... the scars will be with me forever.
nodes.text: Bila je velika sreća imati uz sebe prijatelje i obitelj koji su mi pružali podršku. Kad čitam svoj zapis od 14. travnja 2005., stvarno me dirne. Borba s rakom oduzela je velik dio mojeg života, a njezine posljedice, posebno financijske, još osjećam. Tijelo je prošlo mnogo toga i samo će vrijeme pokazati hoće li neke trajne tegobe nestati. Ožiljci će ostati zauvijek.

nodes.source: 21st April 2006 - Friday
nodes.text: 21. travnja 2006. - petak

nodes.source: Routine blood tests and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danas rutinske krvne pretrage i susret s konzultantom u bolnici Charing Cross.

nodes.source: I watched my blood test again, every detail, I'm getting used to this now! 4 test tubes of blood taken. One and most importantly for my tumour markers (HCG), two to monitor my general health (U&E's & FBC) and finally one for my testosterone levels.
nodes.text: Opet sam gledao vađenje krvi, baš svaki detalj. Sad se već navikavam! Uzeli su četiri epruvete. Jednu, najvažniju, za tumorski biljeg HCG, dvije za opće zdravlje (ureju, elektrolite i kompletnu krvnu sliku) te posljednju za testosteron.

nodes.source: My Consultant diagnosed something new for me today! It was mentioned briefly and has most likely been with me all of my life. The diagnosis is made most often following routine screening blood tests which unmask 'hyperbilirubinemia'. It's named Gilbert's Syndrome and affects between 3 to 7% of the population, with males predominating over females. I'll have to do some more research but this may tick a lot of boxes for me and answer a lot of health related issues. If I wasn't already trying to live a healthier life, I'm going to have to try even harder now!
nodes.text: Konzultant mi je danas postavio još jednu dijagnozu! Samo je kratko spomenuta, a vjerojatno je imam cijeli život. Najčešće je otkriju rutinskim krvnim pretragama koje pokažu hiperbilirubinemiju. Zove se Gilbertov sindrom i zahvaća između tri i sedam posto stanovništva, češće muškarce nego žene. Morat ću to još istražiti jer bi moglo objasniti mnoge moje zdravstvene nedoumice. Ako se dosad nisam dovoljno trudio živjeti zdravo, sada ću se morati potruditi još više!

nodes.source: My lungs are still looking good, X-Ray results show scarring and gristle left in my lungs from the Cancer's demise, some of which may stay with me for the rest of my life. There were some pretty big tumours in my lungs, some the size of apples! Got the routine physical examination out of the way and off I went!
nodes.text: Pluća mi i dalje izgledaju dobro. Rendgenski nalazi pokazuju ožiljke i zaostalo vlaknasto tkivo nakon uništenja raka, od čega će nešto možda ostati zauvijek. U plućima sam imao prilično velike tumore, neke veličine jabuka! Obavio sam rutinski tjelesni pregled i otišao.

nodes.source: 22nd April 2006 - Saturday
nodes.text: 22. travnja 2006. - subota

nodes.source: Today I had my Willow Foundation special day. A fantastic day out, driving exotic sports cars! A small group of us (Ken, my Dad and me) went down to a track in Oxfordshire and all had a go, courtesy of Willow. They even gave us some money to have snacks and a dinner afterwards. It was also nice to see Wendy Gough (Testicular Cancer Awareness campaigner extraordinaire) who had kindly written to the Willow Foundation some time back in order for me to be granted this special day. Sponsor the Willow Foundation... they provide fantastic and very special days for young adults who are going through horrible experiences with their health. Having something special to look forward to in the light of serious illness can make the world of difference. A VERY honourable cause.
nodes.text: Danas sam imao svoj poseban dan koji mi je omogućila zaklada Willow Foundation. Fantastičan izlet uz vožnju egzotičnih sportskih automobila! Nas trojica, Ken, tata i ja, otišli smo na stazu u Oxfordshireu i svi isprobali automobile, zahvaljujući Willowi. Dali su nam čak i novac za grickalice i večeru nakon vožnje. Bilo je lijepo vidjeti Wendy Gough, izvanrednu zagovornicu osvještavanja raka testisa, koja je prije nekog vremena ljubazno pisala zakladi kako bih dobio taj poseban dan. Podržite Willow Foundation! Omogućuju čudesne, posebne dane mladim odraslim ljudima koji prolaze kroz strašna zdravstvena iskustva. Imati nešto posebno čemu se možete radovati tijekom teške bolesti može značiti nevjerojatno mnogo. ZAISTA plemenita svrha.

nodes.source: June 2006
nodes.text: Lipanj 2006.

nodes.source: 23rd June 2006 - Friday
nodes.text: 23. lipnja 2006. - petak

nodes.source: Routine blood tests and X-Ray today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danas rutinske krvne pretrage i rendgen u bolnici Charing Cross.

nodes.source: I watched my blood test again, every detail, I'm an old hand at this! 3 test tubes of blood taken. One test is for my tumour markers (HCG), two to monitor my general health (U&E's & FBC) and finally one for my testosterone levels. The Phlebotomist forgot to take a 4th tube today so instead of sticking me with a needle again he said he would split one of the tubes of blood in to two!
nodes.text: Opet sam pratio svaki detalj vađenja krvi. Sad sam već stari znalac! Uzeli su tri epruvete. Jedna pretraga provjerava HCG, dvije opće zdravlje (ureju, elektrolite i kompletnu krvnu sliku), a posljednja testosteron. Djelatnik je zaboravio uzeti četvrtu epruvetu pa je, umjesto da me ponovno bode, rekao da će podijeliti krv iz jedne epruvete u dvije!

nodes.source: I saw my Consultants understudy today, a Registrar, usual routine, all looks OK so far and the physical examination went OK. The Registrars change from time to time it seems like they do around 6 months stints at different hospitals. My Consultant Dr. Savage still had time to say hello which is always nice, I much prefer to see him over a stranger who really hasn't had anything to do with my case. When you mention something to a new Registrar they scrabble through your file unwittingly to find the answers!
nodes.text: Danas me primio zamjenik mojeg konzultanta, specijalizant. Uobičajena rutina, zasad sve izgleda u redu i tjelesni pregled prošao je dobro. Čini se da se specijalizanti mijenjaju otprilike svakih šest mjeseci, radeći u različitim bolnicama. Moj konzultant, dr. Savage, ipak je stigao pozdraviti me, što je uvijek lijepo. Mnogo više volim vidjeti njega nego nepoznatu osobu koja nije sudjelovala u mojem liječenju. Kad novom specijalizantu nešto spomenete, nespretno kopa po kartonu tražeći odgovor!

nodes.source: I managed a look at my X-Ray, it's a daunting thought each time I have an X-Ray, waiting for the image to appear on screen and hoping that it looks -in my limited capacity as a patient- almost clear.
nodes.text: Uspio sam pogledati rendgensku snimku. Svaki put me plaši čekanje da se slika pojavi na zaslonu i nada da će, koliko to ja kao pacijent mogu procijeniti, izgledati gotovo čisto.

nodes.source: Here's an update of recent symptoms...
nodes.text: Evo novosti o nedavnim simptomima...

nodes.source: Tiredness
nodes.text: Umor

nodes.source: (stamina back to normal now)
nodes.text: (izdržljivost se sada vratila u normalu)

nodes.source: Peripheral Neuropathy
nodes.text: Periferna neuropatija

nodes.source: (gone)
nodes.text: (prestalo)

nodes.source: Tinnitus
nodes.text: Tinitus

nodes.source: (apparent at all times, got used to it)
nodes.text: (stalno prisutno, naviknuo sam se)

nodes.source: Tiger stripes on skin
nodes.text: Tigrove pruge na koži

nodes.source: (still apparent, fading)
nodes.text: (još prisutno, slabi)

nodes.source: Lung twinges/pains
nodes.text: Probadajuća bol u plućima

nodes.source: (occasional)
nodes.text: (povremeno)

nodes.source: Headaches
nodes.text: Glavobolje

nodes.source: (nothing out of the ordinary)
nodes.text: (ništa neobično)

nodes.source: Not much to moan about in the light of things and of course I have my life!
nodes.text: Kad se sve uzme u obzir, nemam se na što mnogo žaliti. I, naravno, imam svoj život!

nodes.source: Financially it is still a huge struggle. I had my garage broken in to last month, lost two mountain bikes amongst other possessions. The insurance company dashed my hopes of them being covered so there's another dent in my ability to get fit again.
nodes.text: Financijski se još jako borim. Prošlog mjeseca provalili su mi u garažu i ukrali dva brdska bicikla, među ostalim stvarima. Osiguranje je srušilo moje nade da je krađa pokrivena policom, pa je to još jedan udarac mojim nastojanjima da se vratim u formu.

nodes.source: August 2006
nodes.text: Kolovoz 2006.

nodes.source: 18th August 2006 - Friday
nodes.text: 18. kolovoza 2006. - petak

nodes.source: Arrived promptly and got the routine blood tests out of the way. After speaking with my Consultant and complaining of some chest pains that were worrying me he recommended an X-Ray, although he was quite positive that there was nothing to worry about. So if I don't hear anything and there are no further updates on the subject then take that as good news... no news is good news!
nodes.text: Stigao sam na vrijeme i brzo obavio rutinske krvne pretrage. Razgovarao sam s konzultantom i požalio se na bolove u prsima koji su me zabrinjavali. Preporučio je rendgen, premda je bio prilično uvjeren da nema razloga za brigu. Ako ništa više ne čujete i ne bude novih vijesti o tome, shvatite to kao dobru vijest. Nema vijesti, dobre vijesti!

nodes.source: It seems these days that any little pains or niggles can sometimes worry me on a large scale. I tend to keep the worries locked up inside too, feeling that others around have probably had enough of me complaining!
nodes.text: Čini se da me danas i najmanji bol ili neugoda katkad mogu jako zabrinuti. Brige uglavnom držim u sebi jer imam osjećaj da je ljudima oko mene već dosta mojeg prigovaranja!

nodes.source: This test in particular I was almost "looking forward to" and for a long time I haven't felt as worried as I did preceding this test. My Consultant was very re-assuring and had pretty much laid my mind to rest by the time I left his room.
nodes.text: Ovu sam pretragu gotovo 'iščekivao', a već dugo se prije pregleda nisam osjećao tako zabrinuto. Konzultant me jako umirio i dok sam izlazio iz njegove ordinacije, već sam bio mnogo mirniji.

nodes.source: Bumped into a lovely couple in the clinic waiting room who I hope I will see again one day. I was recognised from this website! They had sat up and read the entire diary the night before. I stayed and chatted for a while and hope I was of some encouragement to them both, especially Theo.
nodes.text: U čekaonici sam sreo divan par za koji se nadam da ću ga ponovno vidjeti. Prepoznali su me po ovoj web-stranici! Večer prije ostali su budni i pročitali cijeli dnevnik. Ostao sam neko vrijeme razgovarati s njima i nadam se da sam ih ohrabrio, osobito Thea.

nodes.source: Theo, I wish you all the very best in your continued treatment and recovery. Stay as positive as you can and keep in touch.
nodes.text: Theo, želim ti sve najbolje u nastavku liječenja i oporavka. Ostani što pozitivniji i javi se.

nodes.source: I chose not to look at the X-Ray today, it wasn't a routine one, normally I always try to sneak a peek at it. It was just how I felt.
nodes.text: Danas sam odlučio ne pogledati rendgensku snimku. Nije bila rutinska, a inače uvijek pokušam kriomice baciti pogled. Jednostavno sam se tako osjećao.

nodes.source: 31st August 2006 - Thursday
nodes.text: 31. kolovoza 2006. - četvrtak

nodes.source: No news at all from the Doc. So that must be good news!
nodes.text: Od liječnika nikakvih vijesti. To mora značiti da je sve dobro!

nodes.source: I'm abroad at the moment and awaiting Hurricane John to hit, just on the coast of San Jose Del Cabo, Mexico. Reports are that it is a Category 4 storm which can be life threatening. The eye of the storm is predicted to touch down very close indeed!
nodes.text: Trenutačno sam u inozemstvu i čekam dolazak uragana John na obalu blizu San José del Caba u Meksiku. Prema izvještajima riječ je o oluji četvrte kategorije, opasnoj po život. Predviđaju da će oko uragana proći vrlo blizu!

nodes.source: Well I've dealt with a life threatening illness let's see how I cope with this, a different experience indeed, but I have a very positive outlook.
nodes.text: Već sam se nosio s bolešću opasnom po život, pa ćemo vidjeti kako ću se snaći s ovim. Sasvim drukčije iskustvo, ali zadržavam vrlo pozitivan pogled.

nodes.source: Back soon! I hope.
nodes.text: Vraćam se uskoro! Nadam se.

nodes.source: February 2007 9th February 2007 - Friday
nodes.text: Veljača 2007. - 9. veljače 2007., petak

nodes.source: Today it was confirmed that I am officially 2 years clear of Cancer. Every year further away from it all, the better. What fantastic news for me.
nodes.text: Danas je potvrđeno da sam službeno dvije godine bez raka. Što se više udaljavam od svega toga, to bolje. Kakve fantastične vijesti za mene.

nodes.source: I feel my diary must come to an end now and I must move on with my life.
nodes.text: Mislim da sada moram završiti dnevnik i nastaviti sa životom.

nodes.source: Has it changed me. Honestly? Yes and No! Life has not changed one bit, just the way I perceive things have. If anything life is a little harder but I now have a coping mechanism to help guide me through the bad times. I must say though when the good times are good, they are even more appreciated than before.
nodes.text: Je li me sve to promijenilo? Iskreno? I da i ne! Život se nije nimalo promijenio, samo moj način gledanja na njega. Ako išta, život je malo teži, ali sada imam način kako se nositi s lošim vremenima. A kad je dobro, to cijenim mnogo više nego prije.

nodes.source: There probably isn't a day that goes by that I don't see something in the world that lights up my day, mostly it is the person closest to me and other times it's something in the world that you have come to appreciate, more so since the illness.
nodes.text: Vjerojatno ne prođe dan a da ne primijetim nešto što mi ga uljepša. Najčešće je to osoba koja mi je najbliža, a katkad nešto u svijetu što sam nakon bolesti naučio više cijeniti.

nodes.source: Every single day I think about the fact that I have had Cancer, the tinnitus I get reminds me of all of the chemicals pumped through my body and the twinges and occasional -normal- coughs remind me of the Cancer more so than anything else. The scars I have are fading, like memories fading in to the distance.
nodes.text: Svakoga dana pomislim na to da sam imao rak. Zujanje u ušima podsjeća me na sve kemikalije koje su prolazile mojim tijelom, a probadanja i povremeni sasvim normalni kašalj više me od svega podsjećaju na rak. Ožiljci blijede, baš kao uspomene koje se polako udaljavaju.

nodes.source: The times I remember the most whilst in hospital are the days of my illness that will stick with me forever and are some of the most intimate in my life, those that I shared them with will certainly not forget.
nodes.text: Najviše pamtim dane provedene u bolnici, razdoblje bolesti koje će zauvijek ostati sa mnom. To su bili neki od najintimnijih trenutaka mojeg života i oni koji su ih dijelili sa mnom sigurno ih neće zaboraviti.

nodes.source: Something I never spoke about in my diary was the fact that the patients I met in the first male ward I was admitted to, either passed away around me or shortly after I had made their acquaintance. That was tough for me to deal with as at that stage I did not fully understand the likely outcome of my illness, so being surrounded by other people dying of a disease similar to mine was terrifying. I have come to understand Cancer is a very broad term!
nodes.text: O nečemu nikad nisam pisao u dnevniku: pacijenti koje sam upoznao na prvom muškom odjelu na koji su me primili umrli su dok sam bio ondje ili nedugo nakon našeg upoznavanja. To mi je bilo vrlo teško, jer tada još nisam potpuno razumio kakav bi mogao biti ishod moje bolesti. Bilo je zastrašujuće biti okružen ljudima koji umiru od bolesti slične mojoj. S vremenom sam shvatio da je rak vrlo širok pojam!

nodes.source: I think the night and morning before my operation were the most terrifying moments for me, I could not control my emotions and they were laid bare for all to see. The moment the lift doors closed to take me up to surgery was quite honestly one of the hardest things I have ever experienced as I thought I would never see anyone ever again.
nodes.text: Mislim da su noć i jutro prije operacije bili najstrašniji trenuci. Nisam mogao kontrolirati osjećaje i svi su ih mogli vidjeti. Trenutak kad su se vrata dizala zatvorila i odvela me prema operacijskoj sali bio je iskreno jedan od najtežih u mojem životu, jer sam mislio da više nikada nikoga neću vidjeti.

nodes.source: I still get upset now if I think about it too much.
nodes.text: I danas me to rasplače ako previše razmišljam o tome.

nodes.source: Financially I still find things hard, scrambling back to financial health has been a battle in itself and has certainly pulled me down. Testosterone levels and low feelings at times also have affected the way I handle my life. In fact right now I am going through a sudden and difficult personal time and finding it very hard to deal with. Sometimes we just cannot understand what awaits us in life.
nodes.text: Financijski mi je i dalje teško. Borba za financijski oporavak bila je zasebna bitka koja me ozbiljno iscrpila. Razine testosterona i razdoblja lošeg raspoloženja također su utjecali na moj način suočavanja sa životom. Upravo sada prolazim kroz iznenadno i teško osobno razdoblje s kojim se jedva nosim. Ponekad jednostavno ne možemo shvatiti što nas u životu čeka.

nodes.source: Still, I'm a survivor, am thankful for it and you can be too!
nodes.text: Ipak, preživio sam, zahvalan sam na tome, a možete i vi!

nodes.text: Tri godine bez raka, još samo dvije!
